content:
kevin: Hey team — Acme reported a big jump in API p99 for US-EAST clients starting ~09:02 UTC. They said requests are being routed to eu-west and latency jumps from ~80ms to ~420ms. Example trace attached. Can someone take a look?

maya: copying in eng-sre. Can you paste the trace id and a sample request?

kevin: trace id: trace-0b7c4a. Sample curl they ran:```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-live-xxxx' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"gptx-3.1","input":"hi"}'
```
They included a trace snippet showing egress path: `us-east-1 -> edge-proxy -> eu-west-1 -> model-pool`.

raj: interesting. I just checked route-proxy logs for that time window. There's a small window where affinity lookup fell back to global fallback policy because the local affinity table returned a 404. I see a canary rollout of route-proxy v2.3.1 at 09:00 UTC. ops-bot deploy event follows: `deploy route-proxy v2.3.1 -> 09:00:12 UTC (canary)`.

lucy: was there any capacity or node-replacement activity in us-east around the same time? Autoscaler churn can trigger affinity rebuilds.

raj: autoscaler did evict one node for GPU reclaim at 08:58 UTC and rejoined at 09:05 UTC. That, combined with a ttl expiry in the affinity cache (5s) and a buggy path where lookup+refresh race hits the global fallback, could explain cross-region handoff.

maya: can we confirm from customer-facing routing traces? kevin, can you ask Acme for a raw traceroute or the full X-Redwood-Trace header? If they can share the header I can map hops to our edge pools.

kevin: asked the customer, they shared header: `X-Redwood-Trace: trace-0b7c4a/3f2c`. Also sharing their app logs: `request_id=acme-1123 latency_ms=422 routed_region=eu-west-1`.

raj: pulling internal trace for trace-0b7c4a... (short) internal trace shows: `client -> edge-us-east-agg1 -> edge-us-east-agg1 (lookup) -> route-proxy-canary -> fallback-router -> egress-eu-west-1`. So route-proxy canary returned a fallback route unexpectedly.

maya: that suggests the canary path has a codepath that treats missing affinity as global fallback instead of retrying local region. We should rollback the canary and patch the lookup logic.

ops-bot: Notice: Rollback requested for route-proxy v2.3.1 canary. Initiating automated rollback policy 3: revert canary traffic.

lucy: I'll also increase affinity-cache ttl to 30s on a few frontends for short mitigation and add a temporary rule to prefer local-region endpoints for tokens originating from region us-east for 1h.

kevin: customer confirmed latency returned to baseline after 09:10 UTC. They're asking for root cause and mitigation steps to share in their postmortem.

maya: Action items: 1) raj to file a bug on route-proxy fallback logic and include trace & logs. 2) lucy to apply temporary cache/route override and monitor. 3) ops to confirm rollback fully completed and document the canary gating issue. 4) kevin to draft customer note explaining root cause and mitigation.

raj: filed bug RDW-4578: route-proxy canary fallback on missing affinity -> global egress. Attached traces + minimal repro.

lucy: I've pushed the cache ttl change to 5 frontends and added the temporary token-based routing override. Monitoring p99 across us-east now.

ops-bot: Rollback complete for route-proxy v2.3.1 canary at 09:12:34 UTC.

kevin: thanks all. I'll send the customer a concise timeline + what we changed. cc @maya for technical confirmation before I send.

maya: looks good. Recommend calling out the canary rollback and cache mitigation. Also include the follow-up: improved canary gating and affinity lookup retries.

kevin: will do. Closing thread once note is sent. :thumbsup:
